text:
carla: Hey team — getting p95/p99 latency spikes for tenant acme-app since ~23:10 UTC. Support ticket #5231. Customers seeing timeouts and occasional 502s. Observability shows sustained GPU memory pressure on a subset of runtime nodes and a few OOM kills. Any ideas if this ties to the recent allocator rollout?

mohit: Thanks for the heads up. Which model + route? Any route IDs or recent config changes?

carla: route: /gen/v1/tenants/acme, model: redwood/open-small-v3 (4-bit), heavy long-context prompts. I linked Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.infra/d/abcd/tenant-acme-latency — p95 jumped from ~120ms -> ~1200ms, p99 to ~4s around 23:12.

ryan: ops-bot flagged OOMs on gpu-prod-77 at 2024-04-03T23:12Z. Quick kernel logs: 

```
[kernel] Out of memory: Kill process 4123 (runtime) score 987 or sacrifice child
runtime[4123]: kv_cache_size=18.2GB
runtime[4123]: allocator: slab_fragmentation=0.74
runtime[4123]: process 4123 killed by OOM
```

anna: Looks like KV cache grew and slab fragmentation high (0.74). Our slab compact backoff was temporarily set conservative in the March rollout — that could explain slower reclaim.

support-eng: Can oncall grab pprof/heap snapshots for the window 23:00-23:20 and `nvidia-smi` output + dmesg? We'll need alloc histograms and kv entry TTL distribution.

mohit: Running quick probe now — copying commands for reproducibility: 
```
kubectl exec -n runtime -it pod/runtime-77 -- bash -c "python /opt/runtime/scripts/dump_memory_profile.py --since 2024-04-03T23:00 --until 2024-04-03T23:20 > /tmp/alloc.prof"
kubectl cp runtime/runtime-77:/tmp/alloc.prof ./alloc.prof
kubectl exec -n runtime runtime-77 -- nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used --format=csv
kubectl logs -n runtime runtime-77 --since=2h | grep -i oom
```

mohit: Inspecting alloc.prof — high retention in many small KV entries with TTLs < 5s; churn is causing fragmentation and effective usable memory dropped (lots of small holes). Suggest immediate mitigations while we investigate root cause: 
- reduce batch_size to 1 for the route (reduces transient KV pressure)
- enable more aggressive eviction: kv.max_entries -> 400000 (from 500000)
- route traffic to smaller model variant for heavy long-context jobs (fallback)

carla: Can we patch the per-route config quickly? I can coordinate customer-facing comms.

ryan: I'll roll a quick canary to set batch_size_override=1 for /gen/v1/tenants/acme and add fallback-model=redwood/open-small-v2. Doing a 3-host canary first.

ops-bot: deploy started for route acme /gen/v1 -> config: {"batch_size_override":1, "fallback_model":"redwood/open-small-v2"} by ryan

ryan: Canary succeeded on 3/3 hosts, promoting to all hosts.

ops-bot: deploy succeeded on 6/6 hosts.

mohit: After deploy, p95 dropped to ~130ms within ~4 minutes; p99 around ~650ms. No additional OOMs reported on gpu-prod-77. KV growth trend slowed but not fully stabilized.

anna: Good short-term. For medium-term: propose allocator tuning in staging — enable slab_compact aggressive mode and reduce jemalloc purge interval. We'll also add a heuristic to auto-throttle batch_size when slab_fragmentation > 0.6.

support-eng: Action items:
- create postmortem note for #5231 and link timeline + customer comms
- schedule controlled test of allocator flags in staging (mohit owns)
- implement a runtime healthcheck that triggers per-route batch throttling when slab_frag high (ryan owns)
- add a Grafana alert for kv_cache growth rate > X GB / 10m for tenant routes

carla: Customer updated and acknowledged. They're ok with fallback model temporarily. Marking incident mitigated but leaving this thread open for allocator follow-up and postmortem edits.

ops-bot: Incident marked mitigated (automated) — follow-up task #987 assigned to moh it for allocator tuning.

mohit: I'll start a staging experiment tomorrow: flags to flip: slab_compact=aggressive, jemalloc:purge_interval=30s, kv.eviction_alpha=1.2. Will post results here.

ryan: Also adding per-route quick config to enforce batch_size caps so a single tenant can't saturate KV. Will PR today.

anna: Thanks everyone — closing from support side once postmortem and next-step tickets are created.
